scene.source: real SWOT L2 LR SSH Expert + OSCAR L4 currents, Arabian Sea, 55-75E/0-25N, 2024-05-17 to 2024-08-17 -- refreshed live from whatever local granules were present at run time (2026-10-09 14:41 UTC)
scene.note: Irregular real revisit cadence, not fixed-daily: SWOT passes 1-5.5 days apart.

detection.note: No ground truth exists for real satellite data, so this is a count, not an accuracy score against a known answer.

forecast.note: No ground-truth future position exists for real data either; confidence/fit_r2 are the model's own self-assessment of forecast reliability, not an error score.

rl.note: RL eval numbers are from the last time the PPO agent was (re)trained/evaluated -- refreshing real data does not retrain RL automatically, since that takes ~2-3 minutes vs. seconds for detection/tracking/forecasting. With the 93-day real OSCAR series (211 tracks, 123 multi-point, longest 17 days -- a real, substantial replay set, not the earlier 5-episode placeholder), real replay success is low and nearly tied across all three policies (PPO ~2.4%, direct ~3.3%, random ~2.4%): the real task is hard, and PPO doesn't show a clear advantage over the hand-coded baseline here even though it roughly matches it procedurally (27% vs 27.5%). That's an honest result, not a bug -- most real tracks are still short (median length 3), so most replay episodes end before a pursuit has time to play out regardless of policy quality.
